legacy_root.answer: Continue composes an assistant by listing models, rules, prompts, mcpServers (and context/docs/data) in config.yaml, then unrolling each uses: owner/item-name slug through resolveBlock -> registry.getContent -> mergeOverrides (packages/config-yaml/src/schemas/index.ts:113 and packages/config-yaml/src/load/unroll.ts:413). Hub-and-block composition is not a better fit for this program's marketplace than the generated plugin package: the named non-adoptable feature is Continue Hub uses-slug runtime unrolling, which is an opaque passthrough of third-party YAML at load time, the construct A2 refuses (registry additionalProperties false; marketplace_entry requires plugin_id).

block_composition_summary.composition: configYamlSchema lists models, context, data, mcpServers, rules, prompts, docs; each item may be inline or a uses/with/override wrapper. unrollBlocks resolves uses via resolveBlock/registry.getContent and mergeOverrides. A Block in source is the base YAML object plus exactly one of those arrays (blockSchema at index.ts:194). The length(1) singleton is source-only (E3) and is not cited as measured fact.
block_composition_summary.non_adoptable_why: resolveBlock fetches remote YAML by hub slug and merges it into the running assistant. That is opaque passthrough of untyped-to-A2 bytes. A2 generated-SSOT forbids that hatch (additionalProperties false) and binds each marketplace_entry to a plugin_id inside a generated plugin package rather than installing independent hub slugs at runtime.
